Senses.PreferredTarget: the cypress tree in the courtyard
AlternateTargets: the juniper tree before the hall
SearchAliases: cypress tree in the courtyard case

ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: In these records, Zhaozhou Congshen's courtyard-cypress answer blocks both a symbolic explanation and the claim that he merely points to an external scene. It is transmitted as his answer when asked the meaning of the ancestral teacher's coming from the west and repeatedly reopened by later teachers.
EvidenceBody: Dahui Zonggao reports Wuzu Fayan raising the answer and first saying that understanding it in that way is wrong, then repeating it and saying such understanding is right. Xutang Zhiyu transmits the fuller exchange: when the monastic objects that Zhaozhou should not show an external scene, Zhaozhou says he does not show an external scene and repeats the courtyard cypress.

Wansong Xingxiu preserves the further transmission problem in which Huijue denies that his former teacher Zhaozhou ever said it. Ruibai Mingxue stresses that naming the cypress does not present an external scene. Tianran Hanshi warns that descendants die in the words, Hanyue Fazang rejects the explanatory imitation that makes the cypress a display of a cosmic body, and Langting Ting rebukes an answer that merely restates “the ancestral teacher's coming from the west.”

Senses.Note: Seven exact witnesses in seven independent works support one fixed case-answer; later denials and rejected explanations prevent a symbolic tree-gloss or a simple object-pointing account.

Occurrences.Kwic: 五祖師翁舉。僧問趙州。如何是祖師西來意。州云。庭前柏樹子。恁麼會。便不是了也。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Dahui Pujue (大慧普覺禪師語錄): within Dahui Zonggao's later report, Wuzu Fayan raises Zhaozhou Congshen's historical exchange. The formula “Zhaozhou said” (州云) assigns the selected headword token to Zhaozhou; Wuzu owns the later repeated headword token and comment in the full case, while Dahui is only the outer reporter/commentator.

DraftActorProof.SpeechFrame: Dahui's outer report quotes Wuzu's raising; inside it the formula “Zhaozhou said” (州云) assigns this token to Zhaozhou. The later full-case repetition belongs to Wuzu, not Dahui.
DraftActorProof.FullCaseDecision: Zhaozhou owns the selected historical answer token; Wuzu owns the nested raising, later repeated token, and comments; Dahui owns only the outer transmission frame.

Occurrences.Kwic: 趙州因。僧問。如何是祖師西來意。州云。庭前柏樹子。僧云。和尚莫將境示人。州云。我不將境示人。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Xutang (虛堂和尚語錄): Xutang Zhiyu later raises the historical exchange; the formula “Zhaozhou said” (州云) assigns the headword answer and following denial of scene-presentation to Zhaozhou Congshen.

DraftActorProof.SpeechFrame: Xutang raises the case; the formula “Zhaozhou said” (州云) assigns the historical answer to Zhaozhou.
DraftActorProof.FullCaseDecision: Zhaozhou owns the quoted answer and denial; Xutang owns only the later raising/commentary frame.

Occurrences.Kwic: 往來皆謂。僧問如何是祖師西來意。州曰。庭前柏樹子。上座何得道無。覺曰。先師實無此語。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Wansong's Commentary on Tiantong's Book of Serenity (萬松老人評唱天童覺和尚頌古從容庵錄): Wansong Xingxiu reports a saying conventionally attributed to Zhaozhou Congshen by the formula “Zhaozhou said” (州曰), then preserves Huijue's explicit denial that his former teacher ever said it. MasterName records the quoted conventional attribution, not a judgment that the attribution is historically secure.

DraftActorProof.SpeechFrame: 往來皆謂 introduces the conventional report, the formula “Zhaozhou said” (州曰) marks its attribution to Zhaozhou, and 覺曰 assigns the explicit denial to Huijue.
DraftActorProof.FullCaseDecision: The headword token is conventionally attributed to Zhaozhou; Wansong reports rather than authenticates it, and Huijue's denial remains explicit.

Occurrences.Kwic: 解道庭前柏樹子，引得兒孫不丈夫，人人盡向句中死。

DraftActorProof.FullCaseDecision: Tianran owns the critical headword-bearing verse; Zhaozhou is the person discussed.

DraftEvidence.ZenBend: A concrete tree-name becomes a fixed answer whose transmission is tested by denying scene-pointing, rejecting symbolic explanation, and even questioning whether the historical master said it.
DraftEvidence.CounterexampleOrLimit: The transmitted exchange denies showing an external scene, Huijue denies the saying's attribution, and later teachers reject both symbolic and formulaic explanations; no single tree symbolism is licensed.

DifferentThingTest.Reason: All raise and test the same fixed courtyard-cypress case-answer and its transmission.

DraftEvidence.AliasRationale: Aliases cover the tree image, Zhaozhou attribution, and case lookup while preserving botanical uncertainty in an alternate target.

ModifierControls.Finding: 庭前 locates the named tree before the courtyard or hall; later witnesses explicitly deny that location makes the answer mere scene-presentation.

FamilyControls.Finding: The recurring question answered by the courtyard cypress; retained as the case frame.
Shortened tree phrase occurring in commentary, governed as the same case family rather than substituted for exact-headword evidence.
